assumptions.text: If unspecified, support GitHub-Flavored Markdown (GFM) for parsing, plus standard Markdown links ([text](path/to/note.md)) and Obsidian-style wikilinks ([[Note Title]] and [[path/to/note|alias]]).

If unspecified, define canonical note IDs/URLs as the input relative file path without the .md extension (normalized to URL-safe slugs), and treat links without extensions as targeting the corresponding .md file.
If unspecified, tags are sourced from YAML frontmatter key "tags" (array or comma-separated string); inline #tags are ignored unless explicitly requested.
If unspecified, implement full-text search via a build-time generated client-side index (loaded as a static JSON or similar), requiring JavaScript enabled in modern browsers.
The tool will process files from a local filesystem via a CLI interface.
Search will be implemented as a client-side index generated at build time, with no server-side runtime.
The input dataset size is suitable for a personal knowledge base (e.g., <10,000 notes), allowing full client-side search.
The site will utilize a default theme without complex user-defined theming for the MVP.
Advanced navigation visualizations (e.g., interactive graph view) are out of scope for the MVP.
The tool will be a command-line interface (CLI) that processes Markdown files from a local directory.
Search functionality will be implemented client-side, using a pre-built search index, which is consistent with the static site constraint.
The generated static site will be self-contained and compatible with any standard static hosting provider (e.g., GitHub Pages, Netlify) or local file server.
A default, clean theme will be provided. Advanced theming and custom styling are not part of the initial scope.

notes: IDs QX* and AX* are minted for this clarification plan because the capsule’s existing open_questions/assumptions use different ID formats.
If answers are not provided, the AX* assumptions above act as defaults to unblock design/implementation decisions while staying within the static-site constraint.
Prioritizing syntax clarification (QX1, QX2) as these block core parser implementation.
Assuming client-side architecture (AX2) based on non-goals regarding server-side runtimes.
